headline: An AI-capex scare and a live US–Iran oil shock drove risk assets lower into a triple central-bank week.

regions.name: United States
regions.lede: Enter next week defensively. A hawkish-hold Fed, three megacap capex verdicts and the full growth-inflation-jobs trifecta all land inside four days — against 18-month-high yields and a live oil shock.
regions.meta: S&P 7,411.98 · Fed funds 3.50–3.75% · 10Y 4.68% · VIX ~18.7 · all three indices lower on the week (Nasdaq -2%)

developments.title: Megacap AI-capex shock
developments.body: Alphabet and Tesla beat on revenue but spooked investors on spending — Alphabet lifted 2026 capex to a record ~$205bn and posted its first-ever negative free cash flow; Tesla fell 14.5% on a margin collapse. The Magnificent Seven shed ~$787bn Thursday, the worst day since April 2025.

developments.title: Fed decision Wednesday
developments.body: A hold at 3.50–3.75% is near-certain (5th straight), but the risk is asymmetric toward a HIKE (~35% priced; ~80% by September). New chair Warsh won't give forward guidance, so the statement's tone is the whole signal. No projections at this meeting.

developments.title: Yields at 18-month highs
developments.body: The 10Y hit its highest since January 2025 on the oil spike and new tariffs, with some desks flagging a test of 5%. This is the transmission belt compressing equity multiples and pressuring crypto.

developments.title: New Section 301 tariffs
developments.body: The expired 10% global levy is being replaced by country tariffs (10% on UK/EU/Canada/Mexico; up to 12.5% on Japan/Korea) on forced-labor grounds. JPMorgan estimates ~0.2–0.3pp added to the PCE price level.

regions.name: United Kingdom
regions.lede: A two-speed market. Equities are resilient on their energy and defensive tilt, but gilts are the pressure point as a new PM inherits a strained fiscal position. The Bank of England holds Thursday.
regions.meta: FTSE 100 10,736.23 (2nd weekly gain) · Bank Rate 3.75% · 10Y gilt ~5.03% · CPI 2.6% · GBP/USD ~$1.34

developments.title: New PM: Andy Burnham
developments.body: Burnham became PM on 20 Jul (John Healey named Chancellor; Reeves out). His pledge to seek 'flexibility' within the fiscal rules pushed the 10Y gilt up ~8bp on day one to ~5.05%, its highest since late May. He is the 7th PM in a decade — the churn is itself a gilt risk premium, atop record May borrowing (£23.3bn).

developments.title: Bank of England holds Thursday
developments.body: Bank Rate stays at 3.75% — all 70 economists in Reuters' poll expect no change, with the July Monetary Policy Report alongside. The skew is mildly hawkish (8 see a hike this year vs 4 a cut). CPI at 2.6% is above target but far tamer than the US.

developments.title: FTSE resilience
developments.body: The FTSE 100 rose 1.28% on the week (2nd straight gain), sits ~2% below its record and is +17.7% over 12 months. Its heavy weighting to oil majors and defensives means it benefits when crude rises — the mirror image of the US tech-heavy tape.

developments.title: Heavyweight earnings week
developments.body: The biggest UK reporting week: AstraZeneca, four banks (Barclays, StanChart, Lloyds, NatWest), Shell, GSK, Unilever, Rolls-Royce, BAE, LSEG and the miners. Banks have had a strong year on elevated rates; watch net interest margins and loan-loss trends.

regions.name: Europe
regions.lede: The relative haven. Less tech-exposed and with solid earnings, Europe shrugged off the AI unwind — but an energy-driven inflation risk keeps the ECB's next move tilted toward a hike, not a cut.
regions.meta: STOXX 600 ~644.5 (wk +0.46%) · ECB key rate 2.25% (held) · DAX wk +1.08% · nat gas at 3½-yr high

developments.title: ECB holds, stays vigilant
developments.body: The Governing Council left all three key rates unchanged (2.25%), a unanimous vote. Lagarde flagged 'serious developments' in commodities from the US–Iran escalation and is watching second-round effects. Markets price ~23bp of ECB hikes this year; Pictet calls a September hike likely.

developments.title: Defensive outperformance
developments.body: Europe's lower exposure to the mega-cap AI names cushioned it from the selloff that hit the US and Asia. The trade-off: it captured less of the earlier AI-led rally, but right now that defensiveness is a feature.

developments.title: Earnings strength
developments.body: SAP jumped ~9% Friday on a strong cloud backlog; Wolters Kluwer +5%; heavyweight banks (Santander, BBVA, BNP, Intesa) closed sharply higher. Corporate results have been generally robust across the reporting-heavy week.

developments.title: European energy squeeze
developments.body: Natural gas prices rose to their highest since December 2022 as the Middle East conflict disrupted flows — keeping energy-inflation risk live and limiting relief for eurozone sovereign bonds.

regions.name: Asia-Pacific
regions.lede: Asia took the brunt of the AI unwind and carries the most oil sensitivity. Japan's enormous run leaves it exposed to both AI sentiment and crude, while China grinds higher on policy support.
regions.meta: Nikkei 64,584 (-2.77% Fri) · Hang Seng ~24,963 · Shanghai 3,814 · Japan & Korea heavily oil-import dependent

developments.title: Tech-led selloff
developments.body: Tokyo bore the brunt of Wall Street's AI-capex scare — the Nikkei fell 2.77% Friday with SoftBank -7.6%, Renesas -7.2% and Mitsubishi Motors -7.3%. Asian markets carry heavier semiconductor and AI-supply-chain weightings than Europe.

developments.title: Japan's oil sensitivity
developments.body: Japan depends heavily on Middle Eastern crude, so the oil spike hits its terms of trade directly. PM Takaichi's approval is slipping as cost-of-living measures fall short — a domestic overhang layered on the external shock.

developments.title: China grinds on policy support
developments.body: Shanghai and Hong Kong were soft with the global tape, but the policy backdrop is supportive — five-year-plan priorities in AI and consumption, 'anti-involution' reform, consumer-loan subsidies, and an extended US trade truce that averts triple-digit tariffs.

developments.title: Weekend oil relief
developments.body: Reports of a US–Iran pause over the weekend sent crude sharply lower into Monday, easing the biggest pressure point for oil-importing Asia. Durability of the pause is the key unknown.
